Stated Claim / Post Context:
Two teenage boys, ages 13 and 15, identified as victims of horror shooting on California beach that left two more injured

The sheriff's office identified the victims on Tuesday afternoon as Marco Antonio Perez, 15, and Nathaniel Flores, 13. Both of the teens were from Salinas.

Actual Article Body:
By SOPHIE GABLE, US REPORTER

Published:  11:50 AEDT, 4 November 2026   |  Updated:  13:21 AEDT, 4 November 2026

Two teenage boys aged 13 and 15 years old have been identified as the victims in a horror shooting on a California beach that left two others injured.

Marco Antonio Perez, 15, and Nathaniel Flores, 13 were identified as the two victims of a shooting at Moss Landing State Beach just before 2am on Monday, according to the Monterey County Sheriff's Office.

Both teens, who were from Salinas, were found with gunshot wounds. Flores was just days away from turning 14.

A third individual was transported from the scene to a local hospital with non-life threatening injuries, and a fourth victim later arrived at a local hospital suffering from gunshot wounds.

Commander Andres Rosas told the Daily Mail that there are no new details regarding the investigation. Authorities have yet to identify the two injured individuals.

Rosas said the department does not have an update on those who were injured due to patient privacy laws, adding that officers are only notified if there is a fatality.

'Fortunately, we have NOT received that type of update,' he added.

Rosas told reporters that the investigation is ongoing and the victims' deaths have not been officially classified.

Nathaniel Flores, 13, was identified as one of the victims in the shooting. His football league remembered him as a 'son, a teammate, and a friend.' Picture source: GoFundMe

Police responded to the scene of the shooting along Jetty Road in Moss Landing in Monterey County on Monday

Flores played football with the Steinbeck Tigers Youth Football & Cheer organization. Picture source: GoFundMe

'We're not calling this a homicide. We haven't confirmed if this is a homicide or a suicide or any other type of death. We have not made that declaration yet,' Rosas said.

'We are investigating the circumstances under which these individuals died as a result of gunshot wounds here at the scene.'

Rosas told the community that officers do not believe there is an ongoing threat.

State Park Ranger Supervisor Mike Dipple called the shooting 'an isolated incident,' adding that the park would reopen as soon as the crime scene is cleared.

The superintendent of Salinas Union High School District, Dr Zandra Jo Galvan, confirmed that the two victims were students at the school.

'It is with profound sadness and heavy hearts that we share that members of our district student community were among those who lost their lives in the tragic incident that occurred early Monday morning in Moss Landing,' Galvan wrote.

Flores attended Salinas Union High School District and played football. Picture sources: GoFundMe

State Park Ranger Supervisor Mike Dipple called the shooting 'an isolated incident'

The investigation into the shooting is ongoing. The two victims' deaths have not yet been classified by police

The superintendent said the school's hearts were with those grieving the 'devastating loss,' adding that emotional support services would be available for students and staff.

The Steinbeck Football & Cheer program launched a GoFundMe for Flores' family. They shared that Flores played football and was preparing to celebrate his 14th birthday on Friday.

'His unexpected passing has left his family, teammates, coaches, and our entire Steinbeck community heartbroken,' the fundraiser description read.

'Once a Tiger, always a Tiger. Rest in peace, Nathaniel “Nate” Flores,' they added.
